Chilean research institutes and firms refined heap-leach bacteria (Thiobacillus ferrooxidans) and extractant chemistry. Oxide reserves deplete faster than sulphides, so SX-EW output in Chile peaked near 2 million tonnes around 2010 and has since declined as mines return to concentrators.

chinese-room-1980.summary: In 1980 Searle argued that a man following rules to answer Chinese questions understands nothing, and neither does a computer. He imagines himself locked in a room with an English version of some program that handles Chinese, plus pencils, paper and filing cabinets; Chinese characters slip in under its door, he follows his instructions step by step, and slides answers back out. If any computer running that program passed its Turing test, so would he, yet he understands no Chinese. Searle aimed this at functionalism, computationalism and what he calls strong AI.

chinese-room-1980.detail: Strong AI, in Searle’s phrase, holds that appropriately programmed computers thereby have minds. His paper drew an enormous number of commentaries and responses over following decades. Behavioral and Brain Sciences editor Stevan Harnad notes that “the overwhelming majority” still think it “dead wrong,” and arguing over why has filled a literature of its own.

cnn-launch-1980.summary: In June 1980 CNN went on air with news 24 hours a day. Ted Turner introduced it, and husband and wife David Walker and Lois Hart anchored its first newscast. Cable carriage let it reach homes outside broadcast schedules from Atlanta, Georgia. CNN grew to 42 bureaus and over 900 affiliated local stations, made Turner a media mogul and set television news on a round-the-clock footing its rivals later matched.

collingridge-dilemma-1980.summary: In 1980 David Collingridge observed that a technology's harms cannot be known until it spreads, when it is too late to steer it. His book sets out his dilemma of controlling technology, which now bears his name. It has two halves: an information problem, since a technology’s social effects cannot be predicted until it is extensively developed and widely used, and a power problem, since by then it has become entrenched and changing it is costly and slow. His dilemma anchors technology assessment debates.

era-expert.summary: From 1980 to 1987 expert systems, programs built from thousands of hand-written rules, became AI's first profitable business. An expert system answers questions or solves problems within one narrow domain using logical rules drawn from human experts; staying narrow sidestepped commonsense knowledge, and R1, finished at Carnegie Mellon for Digital Equipment Corporation in 1980, was saving DEC $40 million yearly by 1986. “Overall, the AI industry boomed from a few million dollars in 1980 to billions of dollars in 1988.” Then specialised Lisp hardware collapsed in 1987, and expert systems proved brittle and costly to maintain.

expert-systems-boom-1980s.summary: From 1980 corporations bought expert systems that encoded specialists' rules; AI became a billion-dollar industry, then collapsed again. Expert systems encode rules drawn from specialists to answer questions in one domain, and knowledge, rather than search, became mainstream AI’s focus. After R1 began configuring Digital Equipment Corporation’s orders in 1980, companies worldwide built their own, spending over $1 billion by 1985. Its hardware market collapsed in 1987, opening AI’s second winter.

Shu Shien-Siu, minister of science and technology, had toured America, Europe and Japan after 1973 and in 1976 proposed a park modelled on Silicon Valley; former finance minister Li Kwoh-ting consulted Stanford’s Frederick Terman and persuaded engineers who had gone abroad to return, among them Morris Chang, who later led Industrial Technology Research Institute and founded TSMC. Both TSMC and UMC, now the world’s two largest semiconductor foundries, were spun out of ITRI next door.

lisp-machines-symbolics-1980.summary: In 1980 Symbolics was founded and, with LMI, began selling computers built to run Lisp across 1980 and 1981; the AI boom bought them and the AI winter killed them. Richard Greenblatt and Thomas Knight began MIT’s project in 1973, producing CONS and then CADR. In 1979 Russell Noftsker proposed commercializing CADR; his quarrel with Greenblatt split MIT’s AI Lab, and after internal battles Symbolics shipped CADR as its LM-2 in 1981, while Greenblatt’s Lisp Machines, Inc. sold it as LMI-CADR. Perhaps 7,000 Lisp machines were sold in all, before cheaper desktops ended their market in 1987.

orangi-pilot-project-karachi-1980.summary: In April 1980 social scientist Akhtar Hameed Khan begins work in Orangi, an unplanned settlement of hundreds of thousands in Karachi. His team cuts cost of underground lane sewers to about a quarter of contractor rates by simplifying design, dropping contractor margins and letting each lane of 20 to 40 houses organise and pay for its own digging. Households finance latrines, lane sewers and collector drains themselves; government is asked only for trunk mains and treatment. By 1993 lane sewers serve 3,285 lanes, 97 percent of area where OPP had worked since 1982, and an estimated million residents. Hasan's writings make this component-sharing model a reference for sanitation programmes in Pakistan and beyond.

pac-man-1980.summary: In May 1980 Namco released Pac-Man, a maze game with no shooting; it drew women into arcades and sold 400,000 machines. Toru Iwatani led its nine-person team from early 1979, setting out to make a cheerful, nonviolent game that would draw women and couples into arcades then filled with war and sports titles; his round hero came from a pizza missing one slice and from kuchi, Japanese for mouth. Players guide Pac-Man through a maze eating every dot while four ghosts, each with its own chasing habit, pursue him; power pellets turn them blue and edible for a few seconds.

slv-3-rohini-launch-1980.summary: On 18 July 1980 a four stage solid fuel Satellite Launch Vehicle, SLV-3, lifted off from Sriharikota and placed 35 kilogram Rohini RS-1 into low Earth orbit. Project director A. P. J. Abdul Kalam led a team that had built motors, guidance and stage separation in Thiruvananthapuram after a first attempt failed in August 1979. India became sixth country to orbit a satellite on its own rocket. SLV-3 technology, scaled through ASLV, led to PSLV in 1994, workhorse for Indian remote sensing and for foreign payloads, and later to GSLV and lunar and Mars missions.

smallpox-eradication-1980.summary: In May 1980 WHO certified smallpox eradicated, the first disease humans have wiped out. Smallpox killed up to 300 million people after 1900; as late as 1967, 15 million people caught it and two million died. Edward Jenner had introduced its vaccine in 1796, and WHO ran a global vaccination campaign from 1958 to 1977, intensified in 1967, that tracked outbreaks and vaccinated around them until its last naturally occurring case was diagnosed in Somalia in October 1977. Smallpox remains the only human disease ever eradicated.

technion-ubiquitin-discovery-1980.summary: Working at Technion in Haifa, with sabbatical stays in Irwin Rose's laboratory at Fox Chase in Philadelphia, Avram Hershko and his student Aharon Ciechanover show in two 1980 papers that a small heat-stable polypeptide, later identified as ubiquitin, is covalently attached to proteins in an ATP-dependent step that marks them for degradation. Their reticulocyte extract work explains why cells spend energy to destroy proteins and reveals a regulated pathway, not a passive scavenger. Later work maps enzymes E1, E2 and E3 and proteasome. Ubiquitin signalling turns out to control cell cycle, DNA repair and immune response, and drugs such as bortezomib target it. Hershko, Ciechanover and Rose share 2004 Nobel Prize in Chemistry.

toto-washlet-1980.summary: In June 1980 Kitakyushu plumbing maker TOTO launches its Washlet, a toilet seat with a heated surface and a retractable nozzle that washes with warm water at an adjustable angle, developed after years of trials to fix spray position. Earlier imported medical seats had scalded users. It sold a million by 1987 and ten million by 1998; a Cabinet Office survey found 14 per cent of Japanese households had one in 1992 and 80 per cent of households of two or more people by March 2018. TOTO passed 70 million cumulative shipments in November 2025, with overseas sales above 30 per cent in 2024. Japan Society of Mechanical Engineers listed the original Washlet as engineering heritage in 2012.

winner-artifacts-politics-1980.summary: In 1980 Langdon Winner asked whether artifacts have politics and answered yes; a low bridge or a nuclear plant decides who does what. It argues that artifacts can carry politics in two ways. First, a specific design or arrangement can settle an issue in a community: Winner cites Robert Moses’s low parkway overpasses on Long Island, which kept 12-foot buses, and those who rode them, away from Jones Beach. Second, some technologies are inherently political, requiring or strongly suiting particular patterns of power: an atom bomb demands centralized, hierarchical control, while solar energy’s advocates argue it suits decentralized, democratic arrangements.

xcon-1980.summary: In 1980 DEC's XCON began configuring computer orders by rule, the first expert system to earn its keep in daily business. John McDermott of Carnegie Mellon University had written it in 1978 in OPS5 as a production-rule system: each rule says that when an order shows certain conditions, add or adjust a component. Its rules came from DEC’s PDP-11 and VAX experts, who sometimes disagreed among themselves. It grew to 6,200 rules by 1987, half changing every year, and maintaining it became exceedingly difficult, a warning for expert systems generally.

cassava-mealybug-biocontrol-1981.summary: Cassava mealybug, carried from South America in the early 1970s, was destroying a staple that feeds some 200 million Africans. Hans Herren's team at IITA, International Institute of Tropical Agriculture, in Ibadan found a parasitic wasp, Epidinocarsis lopezi, in Paraguay and released it in southern Nigeria in 1981 after host-specificity checks. It spread from seven release areas through Benin and Nigeria into Niger and, by 1990, was established in 24 countries across more than 12.7 million square kilometres. Releases by ground and aircraft followed, with wasps bred by the thousands per second at peak. Mealybug populations fell to tolerable levels without pesticides, a model case for classical biological control.

end-to-end-principle-1981.summary: In 1981 Saltzer, Reed and Clark argued that networks should be dumb pipes with intelligence at their ends; the internet was built that way. Their reasoning is that no network can be expected to match exactly what two communicating programs need, so programs must check and retransmit at their ends anyway; routers and gateways may add such features for efficiency but cannot guarantee them.

hayes-smartmodem-1981.summary: In April 1981 the Hayes Smartmodem let a computer dial the phone with typed AT commands; home computers could go online unattended. Dennis Hayes and Dale Heatherington had been building modems for S-100 computers since 1977; acoustic couplers of that era were dialed by hand, and internal modems worked with only one computer bus. Their Smartmodem plugged into any RS-232 serial port and listened for commands prefixed “AT” on that same line, switching between command mode and data mode on an escape sequence guarded by a pause, so software could dial, answer and hang up on any computer. Nearly all modems since speak some variant of its AT command set.
